questions.question: Which bioterrorism agent requires airborne + contact precautions?
questions.rationale: Smallpox spreads by respiratory and contact routes.

questions.question: A cluster of previously healthy postal workers presents with severe pneumonia, shock, and widened mediastinum. Most likely:
An alert, afebrile patient has double vision, slurred speech, and difficulty swallowing that is progressing downward. Suspect:
questions.rationale: Descending symmetric flaccid paralysis with clear sensorium = botulism.

questions.question: A patient exposed to radiation from a hidden source (no contamination) is:
options: B. Not radioactive — no risk to responders
questions.rationale: Exposure does not make a person radioactive.

questions.question: The most effective first step in external radiological decon is:
options: A. Waiting for a survey meter
questions.rationale: Clothing removal removes most external contamination.

questions.question: A dirty-bomb victim has an amputated leg with arterial bleeding and is contaminated. Priority:
options: C. Tourniquet and trauma care now, decon as part of care
questions.rationale: Life threats first; radiation contamination is rarely immediately dangerous.

questions.question: Doubling your distance from a radiation source reduces your dose rate to:
Potassium iodide is indicated when:
options: C. Radioactive iodine release threatens thyroid uptake
D. For dirty bombs with cesium
questions.rationale: KI blocks thyroid uptake of radioiodine only.

questions.question: Under EPA guidance, the dose guideline for lifesaving actions by emergency workers is about:
questions.rationale: ~25 rem for lifesaving/protecting large populations; higher only for informed volunteers.

questions.question: A patient vomited 30 minutes after a radiation exposure. This suggests:
options: D. A high, potentially severe dose
questions.rationale: Early onset of vomiting correlates with higher dose.

questions.question: You receive a call about a white powder in an opened envelope at an office. Best initial action:
options: B. Shake the envelope to see contents
C. Isolate the area, keep the envelope still, wash hands with soap and water, notify law enforcement/HazMat
questions.rationale: Contain, wash, notify; prophylaxis only if testing confirms a threat.
